title: One Baker Up, One Baker Down
title_candidates: One Baker Up, One Baker Down
Top and Tail: The Bakers Take Both Ends of Catalunya
Forty-Six on the First Day, Then Three Days of Hanging On
A Hundred and Six, and Still the Champion
theme: TEG 18 was won in its first eighteen holes and then spent three days not being given back — and the family that supplied the champion also supplied the Wooden Spoon.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, British English; subverted gravitas, trivial stakes handled with diplomatic solemnity
opening_hook: Open on the image rather than the timeline: Alex Baker on the Stadium 14th in R4 (b25) writing a 10 on a par 4 and still, mathematically, untouchable — then pull back to explain that the tournament had been decided on the Tour course in R1, and that the man finishing 43 points behind him shares his surname.
foreshadow: Alex Baker's 46 in R1 (b40, b47) puts him 12 clear of Patterson — plant that the winning margin was already banked before anyone had unpacked.
Jon Baker takes the Green Jacket lead at the 5th in R1 and holds it into R2 (b48) — the defending Trophy champion looks like the man to beat.
Gregg Williams, the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, opens with a 9 at the 7th and an 8 at the 17th (b24, b20) — plant him as a man on course to keep his trinket.
David Mullin runs up an 11 at the 15th in R1 and drops to the bottom of the Spoon race (b35, b66) — plant the nine-time Jacket winner as a man in freefall.

rounds.chosen_headline: A Ten at the 14th, a Trophy at the 18th
rounds.angle: Alex Baker's closing round is a 38 containing a 10 and an 8 and it is still enough by 8; Williams closes with a personal-best 84 to take the Jacket by 14; Mullin drops nine shots from the 14th to the 17th; Jon Baker signs for 29 and the Spoon.

players.arc: Three prior Wooden Spoons and one in two of the last three TEGs; posts 46 on the first day to bank the entire winning margin, then survives a course-worst 106, an 11, a 10 and an 8 without ever finishing a round worse than 3rd of five — a second Trophy won by refusing to be caught rather than by pulling away.

Defending Trophy champion and holder of the Jacket lead from the 5th in R1, he loses that lead after 20 holes in front (b48), makes a 9 at the 4th in R3 that drops him to the bottom for good, and finishes 23 points adrift of the next worst man — the Spoon collected in the same week his brother collects the Trophy.

The reigning Wooden Spoon holder opens with a 9 at the 7th and an 8 at the 17th, answers with 42 points in R2, takes the Jacket lead at the Stadium 2nd in R3 and closes with a personal-best 84 to win the gross by 14.

An 11 at the 15th in R1 puts the nine-time Jacket winner bottom of the Spoon race; two days later he shoots 84 to break the Stadium course record, then bleeds nine shots from the 14th to the 17th in R4 and loses the Jacket by 14.

Bleeds 22 shots in eight holes on the opening morning, is bottom of the Spoon race by the 4th, and still finishes runner-up on the Trophy with new personal bests on both Catalunya courses — the best week of anyone who never led anything.

venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to Catalonia: two rounds on the Tour course (the 5th and 6th TEG rounds there) then two on the Stadium (the 6th and 7th). Lean on the irony in the course descriptions — the Tour is billed as the more forgiving sibling and it produced the course-worst 106 (cr02), Patterson's 22-shot bleed and Mullin's 11, while the Stadium, 'Spain's premier golf course', gave up the lowest TEG round ever recorded on it (cr01) and two personal-best 84s. Note the switch of venues as the tournament's hinge: both the Jacket and the Spoon were settled in the first two holes of R3, the moment the field moved across.
course_history_notes: Mullin's 84 in R3 was a new personal best at the Stadium, improved by 7 on his prior 91 (TEG 11) — and the course record (cr01).
Williams's 84 in R4 was a new personal best at the Stadium, improved by 8 on his prior 92 (TEG 12), and 8 shots better than his last visit.
Patterson set new personal bests on both courses: 94 at the Tour in R2 and 93 at the Stadium in R3.
The two Bakers went backwards on the Stadium — Jon 8 shots worse than his last visit, Alex 7 worse — while the Jacket contenders went forwards.

trophy_storyline.subject: Alex Baker's Trophy: won in eighteen holes, defended over fifty-four
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: The entire eight-point winning margin, and more, was banked on the first day; everything after it was a man declining to hand it back while golf happened to him.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: 46 points in R1 on the Tour course, best in the field, 12 clear of Patterson before anyone had settled in. Turn: R2 hands him the worst gross round in the course's TEG history — 106, with an 11 at the 18th and an 8 at the 16th — and costs him exactly one point of the lead, and R4 contains a 10 at the 14th and an 8 at the 17th. Resolution: two rounds won outright, never a round worse than 3rd of five, and a closing 38 that was quite bad enough and still won by 8.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams: from reigning Spoon holder to Green Jacket by 14
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: The man who arrived holding TEG 17's Wooden Spoon left with the gross title and a personal best on Spain's premier course, and he built the margin rather than inheriting it.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: R1 is a shambles — a 9 at the 7th, an 8 at the 17th, the bleeding stopped only by a birdie at the 15th — and he is third and drifting. Turn: 42 points in R2, four holes from the 13th without dropping a shot, and then the takeover at the Stadium's 2nd hole in R3, ending Jon Baker's 20-hole tenure in front. Resolution: a closing 84, his best ever round on the Stadium, and the Jacket by 14.

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker: the defending champion who finished 23 points behind the next worst man
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The holder of the Trophy and the Jacket from TEG 17 led the gross for 20 holes and then fell further than anyone in the field, in the same tournament his brother won the lot that mattered.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: leads the Jacket from the 5th in R1 and closes R2 with five holes and 16 points, birdie at the 14th — the best golf anyone played that afternoon. Turn: the lead goes at the 7th in R2, and a 9 at the 4th in R3 drops him to the bottom of the Spoon race at the Stadium's 2nd, where he stays. Resolution: 28 and 29 to finish, last in three rounds of four, 126 points, 23 adrift of Mullin and 43 behind his brother.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin's fortnight of extremes: an 11, then the lowest round in Stadium history
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The same man produced the single worst hole and the single best round of TEG 18, and finished with neither a trophy nor a Spoon to show for it.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: an 11 at the Tour 15th in R1 drops the nine-time Jacket winner straight to the bottom of the Spoon race. Turn: 84 gross on the Stadium in R3 — a new course record, beating the prior mark of 89 across 27 prior visits, and his own best there by 7. Resolution: nine shots gone between the 14th and the 17th in R4, and the Jacket lost by 14 to a man who shot the same number a day later.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson, runner-up, having spent the opening morning going backwards
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The man who came second on the Trophy began the tournament by dropping 22 shots in eight holes and bottoming the Spoon race by the 4th.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 holes 3 to 10 — 8, 7, 7, 6, 8, 6, 7, 7 — 22 shots gone and last in the field. Turn: a back nine 14 points better than his front, 13 points from the 13th to the 16th, and 16 points across five holes in R2 either side of a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 4th. Resolution: personal bests on both courses, a birdie at the 17th in R4, and second place behind a man he outplayed in two of the four rounds.

discovered_storylines.subject: The Catalunya toll: every man in the field signs for at least one 8 or worse
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A resort billed as one of Europe's elite tests was met with a sustained, democratic outbreak of double figures and near-misses, and the champion led the way.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 alone yields Patterson's 8 at the 3rd, Williams's 9 at the 7th and Mullin's 11 at the 15th. Turn: R2 adds Alex Baker's 8 at the 16th and 11 at the 18th, the second of which completes a 106; R3 adds Jon Baker's 9 at the 4th. Resolution: R4 supplies the champion with a 10 at the 14th and an 8 at the 17th, and he wins by 8 anyway — the tournament's governing principle stated in full.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker's 46 in R1 and the 12-point lead
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided — the Trophy section
payoffs.payoff: The final margin was 8: he took 12 out of R1 and gave 4 of them back over the following three days, so the tournament was over before the Stadium was reached.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker leading the Jacket from the 5th in R1
payoffs.payoff: The 20-hole tenure ends at the 7th in R2 (b48) and by the 2nd at the Stadium in R3 he is bottom of the Spoon race for good — from leading one competition to losing the other by 23.

payoffs.seed: Williams's R1 wreckage as reigning Spoon holder
payoffs.payoff: A personal-best 84 on the Stadium and the Green Jacket by 14 — the Spoon handed on to the defending Trophy champion.
The same man shoots 84 to break the Stadium course record (cr01), the lowest gross ever recorded there in TEG.

vehicle_fit_response.note: The blow-up catalogue is real and runs as a discovered storyline (b23/b24/b35/b36/b39/b25), but catalogue framed both TEG 15 and TEG 16; the Baker brothers taking first and last, with the defending champion sliding to the Spoon and the reigning Spoon holder taking the Jacket, is the fresher and truer frame.

why_the_champion_won: One enormous opening round and then sheer refusal to fall over: 46 points in R1 put him 12 clear of Patterson, and over the next three rounds he gave back 1, gained 1 and gave back 4 — he won two rounds outright, was never worse than 3rd of five, and Patterson, who outplayed him in two of the four rounds, could not have flipped it even with an ordinary round in place of his worst.
storyline_note: The Trophy still leads, but the Spoon is promoted to co-lead rather than third billing: the Spoon-taker is the champion's brother and the defending champion, so a single dual narrative covers both ends of the table and the Jacket sits between them.
